title: Editorial: Soundscape, well-being and mental health during/after the COVID-19 pandemic

findings.mechanism: Changes in acoustic environment due to lockdown measures.
findings.quote: The results indicated that the A-weighted sound pressure level (LAeq) of all 14 floors after the lockdown was higher than that during the lockdown.

findings.consequent: Patients' perceived helpfulness of indoor environment for recovery from COVID-19
findings.mechanism: Positive environmental perceptions contribute to a sense of well-being and aid recovery.
findings.quote: Satisfaction with the indoor acoustic environment and odor were significant predictors how patients perceived the indoor environment to be helpful in their recovery from COVID-19.

findings.antecedent: Quiet, well-sound insulated environment with access to positive sounds (natural, music, urban background)
findings.consequent: Perception of privacy, intimacy, and freedom of expression without noise constraints
findings.mechanism: An ideal soundscape provides psychological comfort and control over one's environment.
findings.quote: The ideal soundscape was described as a quiet, well-sound insulated environment, which guarantees access to positive sounds (i.e., natural sounds, music, and urban background), thus resulting in privacy, intimacy, and a place to express themselves without noise-related constraints.

findings.mechanism: Cross-modal sensory integration influences how auditory stimuli are perceived.
findings.quote: found that visual elements can change individuals' perception of sound

findings.antecedent: Superposition of two intrusive variables (sound-light pollution)
findings.mechanism: The combined effect of intrusive variables did not exceed a threshold for reducing tolerance.
findings.quote: but the tolerance limit of participants was not reduced due to the superposition of two intrusive variables.

findings.mechanism: Individual differences and internal states influence the appraisal of environmental stressors.
findings.quote: The findings implied the moderating effects of subjective factors and the restorative effects of natural sounds

findings.mechanism: Exposure to natural sounds facilitates psychological restoration and stress recovery.
